name: Monoethanolamine lauryl sulfate
description: Monoethanolamine lauryl sulfate (CAS 4722-98-9 ), also known as MEA-Lauryl Sulfate, is an anionic surfactant derived from lauryl alcohol and monoethanolamine. It functions as a primary surfactant delivering foaming, cleansing, and emulsification performance. This versatile chemical is used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. In shampoos, body washes, and liquid soaps, it generates dense, stable foam while effectively removing oils and residues from hair and skin. Home care formulators incorporate it into hard surface cleaners and dishwashing liquids. It is valued where consistent degreasing performance and compatibility with other surfactant blends are required for high-quality results. Textile and leather processors use it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove oils and sizing agents. It is also effective at removing contaminants during various pre-treatment stages in industrial manufacturing. In paper manufacturing, it supports fiber dispersion and surface treatment processes. This is particularly useful where controlled foaming and emulsification are operationally critical for the final product quality. Monoethanolamine lauryl sulfate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste. The active matter content commonly ranges around 30–35% aqueous solution, providing a stable base for a wide variety of formulations. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care versus industrial end uses.
